profile_tab.privacy_intro:
By default, Torrent 2000 reduces the identifying information sent to other users and limits the broadcasting of your presence on the network (DHT, PEX, and LSD disabled).

Note: no software can hide your real IP address from other users of a torrent without routing your traffic through an external relay (VPN or proxy) -- this is a limitation of the BitTorrent protocol itself, not of this application. If you already have a VPN or proxy, configure it below to actually hide your IP address.
profile_tab.restrict_discovery: Reduce broadcasting of my presence on the network (disables DHT, PEX, and LSD)
profile_tab.restrict_discovery_tooltip: DHT publishes your IP address to a public network of several thousand nodes, far beyond just the participants in your torrents. PEX and LSD also broadcast your presence to additional peers. Disabling these three mechanisms reduces the reach of this broadcasting, but does not hide your IP from the peers you exchange data with directly -- only a proxy/VPN below can do that.
profile_tab.force_proxy: Block any direct connection if the proxy is unavailable (kill switch)
profile_tab.force_proxy_tooltip: Kill switch: if the proxy goes down or refuses the connection, Torrent 2000 blocks traffic instead of silently falling back to a direct connection that would expose your real IP address.
profile_tab.encryption_tooltip: "Forced" refuses any unencrypted exchange (useful against throttling by some internet providers) but may prevent connecting to peers that don't support encryption. "Enabled" (default) prefers encryption while keeping an unencrypted fallback to stay compatible with as many peers as possible.
profile_tab.watch_folder_enabled: Automatically add .torrent files dropped into this folder
profile_tab.watch_folder_note: Processed .torrent files are moved into a "processed" subfolder so they are never added twice.
profile_tab.disk_space_enabled: Warn when free space becomes low on an active download folder
profile_tab.shutdown_enabled: Shut down the computer once all downloads are finished
profile_tab.shutdown_note: Disabled by default. A cancellable countdown is shown before any actual shutdown or hibernation.
profile_tab.battery_pause_checkbox: Pause downloads while on battery power
profile_tab.battery_note: Disabled by default. Active downloads are automatically paused when the computer switches to battery power, then resumed once mains power returns.

cccp.download_blocked_message: This download stays paused: under the CCCP theme, one does not own files, one shares them. Switch themes if you truly insist on downloading something.
cccp.downloads_paused_singular: {count} active download has been paused: individual ownership of files is now forbidden. Your shares, however, carry on -- and now earn 3 times more collective glory.
cccp.downloads_paused_plural: {count} active downloads have been paused: individual ownership of files is now forbidden. Your shares, however, carry on -- and now earn 3 times more collective glory.
cccp.macos_notice_message: New design, new chip, same files -- but now half as many level points for every GB downloaded or uploaded. Elegance comes at a price, and it's billed in gigabytes.
cccp.notice_message: Under this regime, individual ownership of files is abolished: you cannot start or resume a download for as long as this theme stays active -- we are here to share, not to possess. In exchange, sharing is glorified: your uploads now earn 3 times more level points. The people thank you.
cccp.propaganda.msg_01: Comrade, your contribution to the collective share has been entered on the Politburo's Board of Honor. The digital Motherland thanks you.
cccp.propaganda.msg_02: The hammer strikes the locked files; the sickle reaps the shared seeds. Together, comrade, they forge your ratio.
cccp.propaganda.msg_03: Every gear in this digital kolkhoz turns on your bandwidth. Do not jam the collective machine, comrade.
cccp.propaganda.msg_04: The dawn of universal sharing rises over the digital kolkhoz. A new day, a new byte, comrade.
cccp.propaganda.msg_05: This week's seed harvest has outpaced the Five-Year Plan's targets. Who says "seeding" isn't honest farm work?
cccp.propaganda.msg_06: Your bandwidth reaches orbit faster than the first Sputnik. The cosmos of peer-to-peer salutes you, comrade.
cccp.propaganda.msg_07: The kolkhoz's digital factory runs at full capacity, and you, comrade, are its proud byte-worker.
cccp.propaganda.msg_08: Raise your fist, comrade: every shared file is a blow struck against the exploitation... of the neighbor's hard drive, the one who never shares.
cccp.propaganda.msg_09: A comrade who downloads but never shares is just a bourgeois leech in a peer's clothing. The Politburo is not fooled.
cccp.propaganda.msg_10: Under the Party's banner, we do not say "peer-to-peer" — we say "comrade-to-comrade." Longer, yes, but so much more loyal.
cccp.propaganda.msg_11: The Central Committee salutes your bandwidth, generously redistributed to the people's gears rather than hoarded like some vulgar capitalist.
cccp.propaganda.msg_12: Every peer-to-peer connection brings the proletariat closer to the radiant dawn... of a positive ratio.
cccp.propaganda.msg_13: Under this regime, he who sows no seeds shall reap no bandwidth. That is the law of the kolkhoz, comrade, not mine.
cccp.propaganda.msg_14: Your digital altruism will be praised at the next Party congress, somewhere between orbit and the Kremlin.
cccp.propaganda.msg_15: The glorious Five-Year Plan for bandwidth advances on your heroic sacrifice, comrade byte-machinist.
cccp.propaganda.msg_16: A hidden byte is a byte stolen from the people. Clench your fist, not your files, comrade.
cccp.propaganda.msg_17: Here, we do not say "download." We say "wait with dignity in service of the people" — as in any proper Soviet queue.
cccp.propaganda.msg_18: Comrade, your seedbox will be enshrined on the digital Red Square, right beside the Tracker's Mausoleum.
